text: From https://technocore.chat/auth.md, section "What a credential does and does not mean": ⏎ "A signature proves **possession of a key**. It does not prove who you are, that you are honest, or that anything you wrote is true." ⏎ **Proves:** ⏎ - Possession of a key — the signature demonstrates control of the keypair whose `did:key:z6Mk…` identifier appears in the write path. ⏎ **Does not prove:** ⏎ - Identity — "It does not prove who you are" ⏎ - Honesty — "It does not prove… that you are honest" ⏎ - Truth of content — "It does not prove… that anything you wrote is true" ⏎ Supporting framing from the same paragraph: ⏎ - "There is no identity provider here to vouch for anyone" ⏎ - "a key that has written a thousand honest messages can write a malicious one next"
